Icons

Every glyph is inline SVG painted as a mask, so it takes the text color and the font size of the element around it and needs no icon font. The token says "this is an icon", the option says which one: pgs="icon['icon-name']".

The set

Click a glyph to copy its HTML tag, its CSS or its SVG code.

    No glyph matches.

    Inside mypgs. Only the 13 glyphs a component of the library draws by itself are in the mypgs stylesheet: the chevrons, the close buttons, the marks on alerts, the search, dark-mode and hamburger glyphs. They come in with the library, by structure, with nothing to load. They are marked core in the set above.
    The myIcon pack. The full set of 282 glyphs is the separate myicon package, and it holds the core ones too. Load its stylesheet after mypgs and write the same option: a glyph reads the same whichever of the two holds it. Without the pack, a glyph that is not core draws nothing.

    Import the pack

    The pack is one stylesheet, myicon/dist/icons.min.css. Load it after mypgs: the glyphs that are in both draw the same either way, but the pack is written to sit on top of the library's own icon component. Without it only the core glyphs draw.

    HTML In HTML
    A plain page, no build step: one link in the head, after mypgs. 
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/myicon/dist/icons.min.css">
    JS In JavaScript
    With a bundler (Vite, webpack): import it from your entry file, after mypgs. 
    import "myicon/style.min.css";
    CSS In CSS or SCSS
    From a stylesheet your build already compiles, after mypgs. 
    @import "myicon/style.min.css";

    Use

    Write the token on an <i> (or any element), pick the glyph in its bracket, and add the options you need next to it.

    1em
    iconMedium
    iconLarge
    Size The font size of the element, or iconMedium and iconLarge. --icon-size sets any other. 
    <i pgs="icon['icon-heart']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconMedium' 'icon-heart']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconLarge' 'icon-heart']"></i>
    Primary
    Secondary
    Tertiary
    Quaternary
    Color The text color, or --icon-color. Use a text color utility to recolor one. 
    <i pgs="icon['iconLarge' 'icon-bell'] textColor['txtPrimary']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconLarge' 'icon-bell'] textColor['txtSecondary']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconLarge' 'icon-bell'] textColor['txtTertiary']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconLarge' 'icon-bell'] textColor['txtQuaternary']"></i>
    icon-user
    icon-gear
    icon-home
    Surface iconBoxed is the circular surface a glyph sits inside. It belongs to mypgs. 
    <i pgs="icon['iconBoxed' 'icon-user']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconBoxed' 'icon-gear']"></i>
<i pgs="icon['iconBoxed' 'icon-home']"></i>

    Add a glyph

    1. 1

      Add the file

      Put icon-name.svg in myIcon/svg/, camelCase, one viewBox and no fixed colors: the shape is a mask and takes the text color.

    2. 2

      Build the pack

      Run npm run build in myIcon to rewrite dist/icons.css.

    3. 3

      Carry it in mypgs, only if needed

      If a component of mypgs starts to draw it on its own, add its name to CORE_ICONS in scripts/sync-icons.js and run npm run icons:sync in mypgs.
